tail:
Batch 9’s nine draft items, A/B page metadata, source coverage, dependency evidence, notes, and proof contracts are authored. The A/B page bodies remain empty. The plan and plan-spec agree.

The minimax definition now specifies the probability space and law for learner randomness, its independence from the data, and the product measurability conditions. The assigned items’ dependency levels match the manifest graph.

**Checks passed:** precheck (8 proofs), proof-layout (9 items, 26 steps), rendercheck (11 files), content policy, focused dependency and forward-reference checks, extcheck, strict proof contracts (9/9), and source-fetch verification (6/6).

**Owner-side blockers:** A later batch-37 manifest has 22 string entries where item objects with IDs are required; the run loader fails with `Duplicate item undefined`. This prevents refreshing six Step 1 readiness records made stale by the final definition clarification and blocks live batch-level recomputation. Run-wide proof-contract coverage also encounters the empty `distribution-shift-and-domain-adaptation` inventory; the item-level check reports 112 empty inventories and 18 other item-level mismatches. I left those other batches and the shared scheduling artifact untouched.

See the [batch notes](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/machine-learning-all-101-2026-10-19-batch-9.notes.md), [proof contracts](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/machine-learning-all-101-2026-10-19-batch-9.proof-contracts.json), and [dependency inputs](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/machine-learning-all-101-2026-10-19-batch-9.dependency-inputs.json).
